title: Artefact signing, verification and provenance (SLSA and Sigstore)

videos.script: A tag is a name somebody can move. {{tag}} The registry keeps no record of where it pointed yesterday. So a check that passed on main yesterday says nothing about main today. This lesson gives linkbox's images a name that cannot move. {{digest}} It starts with the digest, a hash of the bytes themselves. Then the CI server gets a key of its own, and signs every digest it pushes. {{sign}} You will watch verification refuse two things. An image that moved under a trusted tag. And a signature made with somebody else's key. {{refuse}} Then the pipeline attaches two signed statements to every image. What is inside it, and how it was built. {{attest}} A small policy turns those statements into a yes or a no, before anything is deployed. Last comes the honest part. How far a pipeline on a laptop climbs the SLSA ladder, and what keyless signing and the cluster would add. {{levels}}
